- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days; true values often dip below forecast.
- Underestimate during sharp upward spikes; model tends to lag or over-smooths momentum.
- Overshoot after a spike by 5–15% in the immediate following days; correct by reducing forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >75% above historical mean, reduce by 10–15% for next 3–7 days.
- Lagged bias: if true outcome is >10% above forecast at day 10+, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for day 10–15.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term volatility; if 3 consecutive days show >10% deviation, reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate the final 5–7 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below true mean of last 5 days.
